chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The will (wasiyyah) is a right/obligation upon every Muslim.'

key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةُ: The will or bequest, specifically referring to the act of leaving a portion of wealth to non-heirs or specific beneficiaries.
key_terms.حَقٌّ: A right or obligation, indicating that it is a due duty upon the individual.
key_terms.مُسْلِمٍ: Muslim, indicating the generality of the ruling applies to all Muslims.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on making a will (wasiyyah) for Muslims?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the will as a fundamental right (*haqq*) incumbent upon every Muslim, reflecting the Shia juristic view that it is a necessary mechanism for fulfilling financial obligations and ensuring equitable distribution beyond statutory heirs. This narration underscores the transition of the will from a mere recommendation to a binding duty in contexts where specific debts or gifts to non-heirs must be settled before inheritance division.
